title: The angle at the centre
goal: I can use the fact that the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference.
teach: The angle that an arc subtends at the centre is twice the angle it subtends at the circumference (on the same side). Radii are equal, so triangles with two radii as sides are isosceles.
tvis: ∠AOB = 2 × ∠ACB.

ex.q: ∠AOB = 130°. Find ∠ACB, where C is on the major arc.

watch: The two angles must stand on the same arc.

qs.hint: Angle at the centre = 2 × angle at the circumference.
qs.steps:
1. Theorem: the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc (∠ at centre = 2 × ∠ at circum).
2. ∠ACB = 156° ÷ 2
3. = 78°

qs.text: Reflex ∠AOB = 260°. Find the angle at C on the minor arc.
qs.hint: The reflex angle at the centre stands on the same arc as C.
qs.steps:
1. Theorem: the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc (∠ at centre = 2 × ∠ at circum).
2. Angle at C = reflex ∠AOB ÷ 2 = 260° ÷ 2
3. = 130°

qs.hint: Angle at the centre = 2 × angle at the circumference.
qs.steps:
1. Theorem: the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc (∠ at centre = 2 × ∠ at circum).
2. 4x + 40° = 2 × 3x = 6x
3. 2x = 40, so x = 20
